---
title: "Extra practice: logistic regression"
---

These exercises go further than the
[Logistic regression](05-logistic-regression.qmd) section of the lab.
Once you've tried them,
check your answers against the
[solutions](../lecture-02-solutions/09-practice-logistic-regression.qmd).

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(medicaldata)
```

The exercises start from the lab's `blood` data.
The last exercise uses `cmv`
from [Extra practice: cleaning and tidying](07-practice-clean-and-tidy.qmd).
We make both again below so this page works on its own.

```{r}
blood <- blood_storage |>
  mutate(
    recurrence = factor(Recurrence, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    rbc_age_group = factor(RBC.Age.Group, levels = 1:3,
                           labels = c("younger", "middle", "older"))
  )

cmv <- cytomegalovirus |>
  mutate(
    cmv = factor(cmv, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    recipient.cmv = factor(recipient.cmv, levels = c(0, 1),
                           labels = c("negative", "positive")),
    donor.cmv = factor(donor.cmv, levels = c(0, 1),
                       labels = c("negative", "positive"))
  )
```

## Exercise 1: Adjust for other risk factors

ds4biomed's model 3 adds `Age` and three more variables.

- `PVol`: prostate volume
- `PreopPSA`: preoperative PSA (ng/mL)
- `TVol`: tumour volume, coded 1 to 3

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

1. Add `Age`, `PVol`, `PreopPSA`, and `factor(TVol)`
   to the lab's model of `recurrence` on `rbc_age_group`.
2. Does storage age now show an association?
3. Interpret the odds ratio for `PreopPSA`.
4. Why are the confidence intervals for `TVol` so wide?
   Hint: `count(blood, TVol, recurrence)`.

```{r}
#| eval: false
rec_fit_adj <- logistic_reg() |>
  fit(recurrence ~ ____, data = blood)

rec_or <- tidy(rec_fit_adj, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
rec_or
```
:::

## Exercise 2: Plot the odds ratios

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

Plot each odds ratio from Exercise 1 with its confidence interval,
on a log scale, with a dashed line at 1.

```{r}
#| eval: false
rec_or |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = ____, xmax = ____)) +
  scale_x_log10()
```
:::

## Exercise 3: The same as `glm()`?

ds4biomed fits these models with `glm()` directly.

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

Fit the lab's model, `recurrence ~ rbc_age_group`, with
`glm(..., family = binomial)`
and compare the odds ratios with the ones from `logistic_reg()`.
:::

## Exercise 4: What does this model ignore?

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

`blood_storage` also has `TimeToRecurrence` and `Censor`.
What does logistic regression leave out?
What kind of model did the original study use?
:::

## Exercise 5: Cytomegalovirus

This is the exercise from ds4biomed's
[analysis chapter](https://ds4biomed.tech/analysis-intro.html).

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

Start from `cmv`, made at the top of this page.

1. Fit a logistic regression of `cmv` on `donor.cmv`,
   `recipient.cmv`, and `time.to.transplant`.
2. Report the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals.
   Which predictor is associated with CMV reactivation?
:::
